title: Ripley's Todd Layhew inducted into Grafton High School Athletics Hall of Fame | Jackson Star and Herald - Ripley and Ravenswood | wvnews.com
text:
GRAFTON, W.Va. — Ripley’s Todd Layhew is considered one of the “most physical football players” in the history of Grafton Bearcat football.
His physicality led to an outstanding career both for the Bearcats and later the Glenville State College (now University) Pioneers. This outstanding play earned him induction into the Grafton High School Athletic Hall of Fame.
Layhew was honored along with five others—Valerie Barlow-Talton, Cameron Gallagher, Brian Cochran, John Bord, and Dan Mankins—in the Class of 2025. The ceremony took place prior to the Bearcats' game on Aug. 30 against rival Philip Barbour in the annual Arch Coal Bowl at McKinney Field on the Grafton High campus.
Layhew is employed by Jackson County Schools, serving as assistant director for the Roane-Jackson Technical Center. This marks Layhew's 36th year in the education field.
Football career highlights
While at Grafton, Layhew helped lead the Bearcat football program to the Class AA state championship in 1984. Layhew was recognized that season as the defensive captain for the Class AA All-State Team. In addition, he was named the Player of the Year for the Big Ten Conference for his work as a fullback/linebacker.
While at Grafton, Layhew also excelled as a wrestler, placing third two consecutive years at the State Tournaments of 1983 and 1984.
After high school, Layhew made his way to Glenville and starred for the Pioneers. He was a four-year starter, playing for two former West Virginia high school coaching legends in Lou Nocida and the late Frank Vincent. He played his first two seasons at Glenville alongside his older brother of two years, Don.
At Glenville, Layhew played linebacker. As a senior, he also started on the offensive side as a tight end. His postseason accolades following his senior season (1988) included being named a Second Team NAIA All-American and an All-West Virginia Conference First Team pick.
Induction and reflections
Layhew reflected on the honor and the bonds he formed with his teammates.
“It was humbling,” Layhew said. “I tried to always be a good teammate. That's the one of things I always tried to be. I feel I should share this with everybody I played with. I know I had really good teammates. A lot of us still get together and hang out.”
Those days at Grafton, and Glenville, were indeed special for Todd Layhew. His induction into the Grafton Athletic Hall of Fame was a special moment, one he will never forget.
Family and legacy
Layhew and his wife, Melissa, a Calhoun graduate, are the parents of a daughter, Lindsey, and son, Luke. The Layhews have four grandchildren (two boys and two girls).
Luke Layhew played three sports at Ripley and earned the school's prestigious Athlete of the Year award. He spent one season at West Virginia Wesleyan playing basketball and was named the Freshman of the Year in the Mountain East Conference that season. He later attended the University of Pikeville and gained NAIA All-America honors as a basketball player.
Staying active in sports, Layhew has been a football official for nearly 20 years.
